  let f : Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) :=

  letI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) :=

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra


/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
  side : relCurve C R → Bool
  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)

lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z

lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)

/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)

/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)

/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
restricted to the piece. -/
noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)

/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):

* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).

Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
structure IsGenerator : Prop where
  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
      nonZeroDivisors
        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)

variable {D}

11	/-!
12	# The support tube: the family support is closed over the base (DDR-4 finiteness input)
13	
14	The geometric half of the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) (`informal/spec-dd-r.md` §3
15	item 4): for a local-equation system `d` on a scheme `X`, the **support locus** — the
16	set of points where the (well-defined, by the ratio law) germ of the local equation is
17	not a unit — is closed in `X`; over a base `S` with `X → S` universally closed (the
18	standing `IsProper C.hom`, base-changed to the relative curve over every test ring),
19	its image in `S` is closed, and the **tube lemma** holds: if the support fibre over a
20	base point `s` is contained in an open `U` (e.g. a union of adaptation pieces), then so
21	is the whole support over a Zariski neighbourhood of `s` — piece isolation Zariski-locally
22	on the base.
23	
24	## Main declarations
25	
26	* `IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset` — the topological tube core: a
27	  closed map, a closed set `T`, an open `U` containing the `T`-fibre over `y` ⟹ an open
28	  neighbourhood `V ∋ y` with `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T ⊆ U` (via `Set.kernImage`);
29	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.unitLocus` / `supportLocus` — the (open) locus where the
30	  equations are germwise units, and its closed complement;
31	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ` — membership reads on ANY
32	  covering member through the ratio law;
33	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.supportLocus_inter_opens` — the per-member trace
34	  `supp ∩ U_x = U_x \ D(eqn x)`;
35	* `Scheme.LocalEquations.isClosed_image_supportLocus`,
36	  `Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` — closed image and the tube, for any
37	  `f : X ⟶ S` with `[UniversallyClosed f]`;
38	* `AlgebraicGeometry.instIsProperRelSndLeft`, `instIsProperRelCurveHom` — **the
39	  licence**: `IsProper C.hom` base-changes to the relative curve over an arbitrary test
40	  ring `R` (the field-keyed instances of `Curve/BaseChangeInstances` generalised), so
41	  `UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution;
42	* `DivisorAdaptation.mem_basicOpen_eqn_of_mem_unitLocus` / `unitLocus_eq` /
43	  `supportLocus_inter_pieces` — the adaptation reads the SAME support: on a piece,
44	  `d`'s support trace is `D(h_j) \ D(f_j)` (through `eqn_rel`, both ways);
45	* `FinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces` — the pieces' section rings are `R`-flat;
46	* `DivisorAdaptation.flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` /
47	  `projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — **the (c1) junction**: a
48	  fibrewise-regular adaptation equation has flat colength over the Noetherian test
49	  ring (the `SlicingFlat` keystone on the piece ring), and a finite colength (the
50	  support-tube finiteness input) is then projective — the two clauses of
51	  `IsCertified` (c1) for the piece `j`.
52	-/
53	
54	set_option autoImplicit false

56	universe u

58	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory
59	open TopologicalSpace Opposite
60	open scoped TensorProduct

62	/-! ## The topological tube core -/
63	
64	section TubeCore
65	
66	variable {X Y : Type*} [TopologicalSpace X] [TopologicalSpace Y]
67	
68	/-- **The closed-map tube lemma**: for a closed map `f`, a closed `T ⊆ X` and an open
69	`U ⊆ X`, if the `T`-fibre over `y` is contained in `U` then so is `f⁻¹(V) ∩ T` for some
70	open neighbourhood `V` of `y`. Take `V := Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ)`, open by
71	`isClosedMap_iff_kernImage`. -/
72	theorem IsClosedMap.exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset {f : X → Y}
73	    (hf : IsClosedMap f) {T U : Set X} (hT : IsClosed T) (hU : IsOpen U) {y : Y}
74	    (hfib : f ⁻¹' {y} ∩ T ⊆ U) :
75	    ∃ V : Set Y, IsOpen V ∧ y ∈ V ∧ f ⁻¹' V ∩ T ⊆ U := by
76	  refine ⟨Set.kernImage f (U ∪ Tᶜ),
77	    isClosedMap_iff_kernImage.mp hf (hU.union hT.isOpen_compl), ?_, ?_⟩
78	  · intro x hx
79	    by_cases hxT : x ∈ T
80	    · exact Or.inl (hfib ⟨hx, hxT⟩)
81	    · exact Or.inr hxT
82	  · rintro x ⟨hxV, hxT⟩
83	    rcases hxV (rfl : f x = f x) with h | h
84	    · exact h
85	    · exact absurd hxT h
86	
87	end TubeCore
88	
89	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
90	
91	attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra
92	
93	/-! ## The support locus of a local-equation system -/
94	
95	namespace Scheme.LocalEquations
96	
97	variable {X S : Scheme.{u}} (d : X.LocalEquations)
98	
99	/-- **The unit locus** of a local-equation system: the (open) union of the basic opens
100	of the equations — the locus where the divisor cut by `d` is trivial. -/
101	def unitLocus : X.Opens := ⨆ x, X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)
102	
103	lemma basicOpen_le_unitLocus (x : X) : X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) ≤ d.unitLocus :=
104	  le_iSup (fun x => X.basicOpen (d.eqn x)) x
105	
106	/-- Membership in the unit locus reads on ANY covering member containing the point:
107	`y ∈ unitLocus` iff the germ of `eqn x` at `y` is a unit, for every member `x` with
108	`y ∈ cover.opens x` (well-definedness across members is the ratio law). -/
109	lemma mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
110	    y ∈ d.unitLocus
111	      ↔ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) := by
112	  constructor
113	  · intro h
114	    obtain ⟨x', hx'⟩ := Opens.mem_iSup.mp h
115	    have hy' : y ∈ d.cover.opens x' := X.basicOpen_le _ hx'
116	    have hu' : IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x') y hy').hom (d.eqn x')) :=
117	      (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy').mp hx'
118	    obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := d.ratio_isUnit x x'
119	    have hyW : y ∈ d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x' := ⟨hy, hy'⟩
120	    have h := congrArg
121	      ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x ⊓ d.cover.opens x') y hyW).hom) hu
122	    rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
123	    rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
124	    exact ⟨u.isUnit.map _, hu'⟩
125	  · intro h
126	    exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨x, (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr h⟩
127	
128	/-- **The support locus** of a local-equation system: the closed set of points where
129	the (well-defined) germ of the local equation fails to be a unit — the underlying set
130	of the divisor cut by `d`. -/
131	def supportLocus : Set X := (d.unitLocus : Set X)ᶜ
132	
133	lemma isClosed_supportLocus : IsClosed d.supportLocus :=
134	  d.unitLocus.isOpen.isClosed_compl
135	
136	lemma mem_supportLocus_iff_not_isUnit_germ {x y : X} (hy : y ∈ d.cover.opens x) :
137	    y ∈ d.supportLocus
138	      ↔ ¬ IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens x) y hy).hom (d.eqn x)) :=
139	  not_congr (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy)
140	
141	/-- **The per-member trace of the support**: on a covering member, the support locus is
142	the member minus the basic open of its equation. -/
143	lemma supportLocus_inter_opens (x : X) :
144	    d.supportLocus ∩ (d.cover.opens x : Set X)
145	      = (d.cover.opens x : Set X) \ (X.basicOpen (d.eqn x) : Set X) := by
146	  ext y
147	  constructor
148	  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hy⟩
149	    refine ⟨hy, fun hyb => hsupp (d.basicOpen_le_unitLocus x hyb)⟩
150	  · rintro ⟨hy, hyb⟩
151	    refine ⟨fun hyU => hyb ?_, hy⟩
152	    exact (X.mem_basicOpen _ y hy).mpr ((d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ hy).mp hyU)
153	
154	/-- **The support is closed over the base**: the image of the support locus under a
155	universally closed morphism (e.g. the structure morphism of the relative curve, from
156	the standing `IsProper C.hom`) is closed. -/
157	theorem isClosed_image_supportLocus (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] :
158	    IsClosed (f.base '' d.supportLocus) :=
159	  f.isClosedMap _ d.isClosed_supportLocus
160	
161	/-- **The support tube** (piece isolation, Zariski-locally on the base): for a
162	universally closed `f : X ⟶ S`, if the support fibre over a base point `s` is contained
163	in an open `U` (a union of adaptation pieces, in the DDR-4 instantiation), then there
164	is a Zariski neighbourhood `V` of `s` such that the whole support over `V` is contained
165	in `U`. -/
166	theorem exists_supportTube (f : X ⟶ S) [UniversallyClosed f] {U : Set X}
167	    (hU : IsOpen U) {s : S} (hfib : f.base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U) :
168	    ∃ V : S.Opens, s ∈ V ∧ f.base ⁻¹' (V : Set S) ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U := by
169	  obtain ⟨V, hVopen, hsV, hV⟩ := (f.isClosedMap).exists_isOpen_preimage_inter_subset
170	    d.isClosed_supportLocus hU hfib
171	  exact ⟨⟨V, hVopen⟩, hsV, hV⟩
172	
173	end Scheme.LocalEquations
174	
175	/-! ## The licence: properness of the relative curve over an arbitrary test ring -/
176	
177	section RelCurveProper
178	
179	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
180	variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
181	
182	/-- **Base change of properness to an arbitrary test ring**: the second projection of
183	`C ⊗ Spec R` is proper, for every commutative `k`-algebra `R` — the general-`R` form of
184	`Curve/BaseChangeInstances.instIsProperSndLeft` (which is keyed on field extensions).
185	This is the DDR-4 support-tube licence over the `Z(♦)`-chart rings `R_Z`. -/
186	instance instIsProperRelSndLeft : IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left :=
187	  MorphismProperty.of_isPullback (P := @IsProper)
188	    (Over.isPullback_left C (overSpec k R)) inferInstance
189	
190	/-- The properness instance, keyed on the `relCurve C R ↘ Spec R` spelling installed by
191	`relCurve.instOver` (definitionally the second projection). In particular
192	`UniversallyClosed (relCurve C R ↘ Spec R)` fires by resolution, which is what
193	`Scheme.LocalEquations.exists_supportTube` consumes. -/
194	instance instIsProperRelCurveHom :
195	    IsProper ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)) :=
196	  inferInstanceAs (IsProper (snd C (overSpec k R)).left)
197	
198	/-- Acceptance smoke test: the support tube applies to the relative curve over an
199	arbitrary test ring with the universally-closed instance found by resolution. -/
200	private theorem supportTube_smoke (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations)
201	    {U : Set (relCurve C R)} (hU : IsOpen U) {s : Spec (CommRingCat.of R)}
202	    (hfib : ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' {s} ∩ d.supportLocus
203	      ⊆ U) :
204	    ∃ V : (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).Opens, s ∈ V ∧
205	      ((relCurve C R) ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of R)).base ⁻¹' (V : Set (Spec (CommRingCat.of R)))
206	        ∩ d.supportLocus ⊆ U :=
207	  d.exists_supportTube _ hU hfib
208	
209	end RelCurveProper
210	
211	/-! ## The adaptation reads the same support, and the (c1) junction -/
212	
213	section Adaptation
214	
215	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
216	variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
217	variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k}
218	
219	namespace FinCoverData
220	
221	variable [IsFinite π] (D : FinCoverData C R π)
222	
223	/-- **Flatness of the piece section rings over the test ring**: each `Γ(D(h_j))` is a
224	localization of a pinned-chart ring, which is free over `R`; the `FinCoverData`
225	companion of `ThetaGeneratorSeed.flat_sections_piece`. -/
226	theorem flat_sections_pieces (j : D.index) :
227	    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.pieces j) := by
228	  cases j with
229	  | inl j =>
230	      exact flat_sections_basicOpen R (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
231	        (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π false) (D.h₀ j)
232	  | inr j =>
233	      exact flat_sections_basicOpen R (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π))
234	        (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π true) (D.h₁ j)
235	
236	end FinCoverData
237	
238	namespace DivisorAdaptation
239	
240	variable [IsAffineHom π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
241	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
242	
243	/-- On a piece, the germ of the adaptation equation is a unit iff the germ of `d`'s
244	tautological equation is (the pointwise refinement clause `eqn_rel`, read at germs). -/
245	lemma isUnit_germ_eqn_iff (j : A.index) {w : relCurve C R} (hwj : w ∈ A.pieces j) :
246	    IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j) w hwj).hom (A.eqn j))
247	      ↔ IsUnit (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens w) w
248	          (d.cover.mem_opens w)).hom (d.eqn w)) := by
249	  obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := A.eqn_rel j w
250	  have hwW : w ∈ A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens w := ⟨hwj, d.cover.mem_opens w⟩
251	  have h := congrArg
252	    (((relCurve C R).presheaf.germ (A.pieces j ⊓ d.cover.opens w) w hwW).hom) hu
253	  rw [map_mul, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply] at h
254	  rw [h, IsUnit.mul_iff]
255	  exact and_iff_right (u.isUnit.map _)
256	
257	/-- On a piece, membership in `d`'s unit locus is membership in the basic open of the
258	adaptation equation. -/
259	lemma mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus (j : A.index) {w : relCurve C R}
260	    (hwj : w ∈ A.pieces j) :
261	    w ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) ↔ w ∈ d.unitLocus := by
262	  rw [(relCurve C R).mem_basicOpen _ w hwj, A.isUnit_germ_eqn_iff j hwj]
263	  exact (d.mem_unitLocus_iff_isUnit_germ (d.cover.mem_opens w)).symm
264	
265	/-- The adaptation's basic opens land in `d`'s unit locus. -/
266	lemma basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus (j : A.index) :
267	    (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) ≤ d.unitLocus := fun _ hw =>
268	  (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j
269	    ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (A.eqn j) hw)).mp hw
270	
271	/-- **The adaptation computes the unit locus**: the union of the basic opens of the
272	adaptation equations IS `d`'s unit locus (so the adaptation and the system cut the same
273	support). Uses that the pieces cover the relative curve (`exists_mem_pieces`). -/
274	lemma iSup_basicOpen_eqn_eq_unitLocus :
275	    (⨆ j, (relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j)) = d.unitLocus := by
276	  refine le_antisymm (iSup_le fun j => A.basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus j) ?_
277	  intro w hw
278	  obtain ⟨j, hwj⟩ := A.toFinCoverData.exists_mem_pieces w
279	  exact Opens.mem_iSup.mpr ⟨j, (A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j hwj).mpr hw⟩
280	
281	/-- **The per-piece trace of the family support**: on the piece `D(h_j)`, the support
282	locus of the family is exactly `D(h_j) \ D(f_j)` — the underlying set of the colength
283	`Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`. This is the shape the DDR-4 finiteness argument consumes: the
284	piece trace of the globally closed (and, over the base, properly closed) support. -/
285	lemma supportLocus_inter_pieces (j : A.index) :
286	    d.supportLocus ∩ (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
287	      = (A.pieces j : Set (relCurve C R))
288	        \ ((relCurve C R).basicOpen (A.eqn j) : Set (relCurve C R)) := by
289	  ext w
290	  constructor
291	  · rintro ⟨hsupp, hwj⟩
292	    exact ⟨hwj, fun hwb => hsupp (A.basicOpen_eqn_le_unitLocus j hwb)⟩
293	  · rintro ⟨hwj, hwb⟩
294	    exact ⟨fun hwU => hwb ((A.mem_basicOpen_eqn_iff_mem_unitLocus j hwj).mpr hwU), hwj⟩
295	
296	end DivisorAdaptation
297	
298	namespace DivisorAdaptation

300	/-! ### The (c1) junction: flat, then finite projective, colengths -/
301	
302	section Junction
303	
304	variable [IsFinite π] {d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations}
305	variable (A : DivisorAdaptation C R π d)
306	
307	/-- **The (c1) flatness clause from fibrewise regularity** (the `SlicingFlat` keystone
308	on the piece ring): if the adaptation equation `f_j` is a nonzerodivisor in every
309	residue-field fibre `Γ(D(h_j)) ⊗ κ(p)`, then the chart-local colength
310	`Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)` is flat over the Noetherian test ring. The fibrewise hypothesis is
311	the seed's `fibre_regular` clause transported through `eqn_rel` (the I-0203 open
312	transport item). -/
313	theorem flat_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField [IsNoetherianRing R]
314	    (j : A.index)
315	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
316	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
317	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
318	        nonZeroDivisors
319	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
320	    Module.Flat R (A.colength j) := by
321	  haveI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) :=
322	    A.toFinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces j
323	  exact Module.Flat.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField hfib
324	
325	/-- **The certificate clause (c1) for the piece `j`**: fibrewise-regular equation +
326	finite colength (the support-tube finiteness input) ⟹ the colength is finite
327	projective over the Noetherian test ring — `IsCertified.finite_colength` and
328	`IsCertified.projective_colength` at `j`. -/
329	theorem projective_colength_of_forall_tmul_residueField [IsNoetherianRing R]
330	    (j : A.index)
331	    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
332	      (A.eqn j ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) :
333	          Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
334	        nonZeroDivisors
335	          (Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
336	    [Module.Finite R (A.colength j)] :
337	    Module.Projective R (A.colength j) := by
338	  haveI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, A.pieces j) :=
339	    A.toFinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces j
340	  exact Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField hfib
341	
342	end Junction
343	
344	end DivisorAdaptation

346	end Adaptation

/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
  side : relCurve C R → Bool
  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)

lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z

lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)

/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)

/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)

/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
restricted to the piece. -/
noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)

/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):

* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).

Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
structure IsGenerator : Prop where
  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
      nonZeroDivisors
        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)

variable {D}

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamily
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction

/-!
# Finite-adaptation extraction: every local-equation system has a chart adaptation
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d))

Every `LocalEquations` system `d` on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` refines to a
finite chart adaptation `DivisorAdaptation C R π d` (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): the two
pinned charts `V₀ᴿ`, `V₁ᴿ` are affine, so the DAT-1 (1f) affine-refinement engine
(`IsAffineOpen.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction`)
produces, for each chart, a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor
points, with a partition of unity. Reindexing each chart family through `Fintype.equivFin`
gives the `Fin`-indexed `FinCoverData`; the equations are the restrictions of `d`'s
equations at the anchors (comparison unit `1`), regular by `d.regular` through the
refinement subordination.

The **certificate** (`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`) is deliberately NOT part of the
extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra
finiteness/flatness hypothesis on `d` (the object of DD-1c's field dictionary and DAT-B's
coverage step, which supply it separately).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divisorAdaptation` — the extraction: `Nonempty
  (DivisorAdaptation C R π d)` for every `d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **Finite-adaptation extraction** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d), the DAT-1 (1f)
pattern): every local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a finite chart
adaptation. The two pinned charts are affine, so on each the affine-refinement engine
produces a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor points with a
partition of unity; the equations are the anchor equations of `d` restricted to the pieces
(comparison unit `1`), regular through the subordination. The colength certificate is a
separate hypothesis and is not produced here. -/
theorem exists_divisorAdaptation (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Nonempty (DivisorAdaptation C R π d) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι₀, _, f₀, an₀, b₀, hsub₀, hpart₀⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  obtain ⟨ι₁, _, f₁, an₁, b₁, hsub₁, hpart₁⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  set e₀ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₀) ≃ ι₀ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₀).symm with he₀
  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁
  -- the `Fin`-indexed cover data
  set D : FinCoverData C R π :=
    { m₀ := Fintype.card ι₀
      m₁ := Fintype.card ι₁
      h₀ := fun j => f₀ (e₀ j)
      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)
      a₀ := fun j => b₀ (e₀ j)
      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)
      partition₀ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₀ (fun i => b₀ i * f₀ i)).trans hpart₀
      partition₁ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₁ (fun i => b₁ i * f₁ i)).trans hpart₁ } with hD
  -- the anchor of each piece and its subordination to a member of `d.cover`
  set pt : D.index → relCurve C R :=
    Sum.elim (fun j => an₀ (e₀ j)) (fun j => an₁ (e₁ j)) with hpt
  have hle : ∀ j : D.index, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) := by
    rintro (j | j)
    · exact hsub₀ (e₀ j)
    · exact hsub₁ (e₁ j)
  exact ⟨DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors D
    (fun j => ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hle j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
    pt hle (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul])⟩

end AlgebraicGeometry

theorem flat_ovlProd_of_seed : Module.Flat R B.ovlProd := by

/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
  side : relCurve C R → Bool
  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)

lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z

lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)

/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)

/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)

/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
restricted to the piece. -/
noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)

/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):

* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).

Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
structure IsGenerator : Prop where
  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
      nonZeroDivisors
        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)

variable {D}

B.toFinCoverData.ovlTermBaseChange_one_tmul p.asIdeal.ResidueField,
      B.toFinCoverData.ovlMap_resHom_left p.asIdeal.ResidueField]
    rfl
  change e.symm
      ((relCurve C p.asIdeal.ResidueField).resHom inf_le_left
        (B.pulledEqn p.asIdeal.ResidueField i)) ∈
    nonZeroDivisors
      (p.asIdeal.ResidueField ⊗[R]
        Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j)) at hback
  rw [hinv] at hback
  have hflip := ringEquiv_mem_nonZeroDivisors
    (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm R p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j)).toRingEquiv hback
  change (Algebra.TensorProduct.comm R p.asIdeal.ResidueField
      Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j))
      ((1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left (B.eqn i)) ∈
    nonZeroDivisors
      (Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) ⊗[R]
        p.asIdeal.ResidueField) at hflip
  rwa [Algebra.TensorProduct.comm_tmul] at hflip

omit [IsProper C.hom] in
/-- Every pairwise overlap colength of a generator adaptation is flat over the base. -/
theorem flat_ovlColength_of_seed (i j : B.index) :
    Module.Flat R (B.ovlColength i j) := by
  let f : Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) :=
    (relCurve C R).resHom inf_le_left (B.eqn i)
  letI : Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) :=
    B.toFinCoverData.flat_sections_pieces_inf i j
  have hflat : Module.Flat R
      (Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) :=
    Module.Flat.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField
      (fun p => B.ovlEqn_tmul_one_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_seed hD i j p)
  have hideal := B.ovlIdeal_eq_span_left i j
  change B.ovlIdeal i j = Ideal.span {f} at hideal
  letI : Module.Flat R
      (Γ(relCurve C R, B.pieces i ⊓ B.pieces j) ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) := hflat
  exact Module.Flat.of_linearEquiv
    ((Submodule.quotEquivOfEq _ _ hideal).restrictScalars R)

omit [IsProper C.hom] in
/-- The product of all overlap colengths of a generator adaptation is flat over the
base. -/
theorem flat_ovlProd_of_seed : Module.Flat R B.ovlProd := by
  letI : forall p : B.index × B.index, Module.Flat R (B.ovlColength p.1 p.2) :=
    fun p => B.flat_ovlColength_of_seed hD p.1 p.2
  exact Module.Flat.pi_of_finite

end Seed

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra


/-! ## The theta generator seed and the `lm:ctn` clauses -/

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
variable {R : Type u} [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsFinite π] {a : ℕ}

/-- **A theta generator seed for a submodule `K ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(Θᵃ))`** (worksheet §3.4.1): at
every point `z` of the relative curve, a pinned chart side containing `z`, a basic-open
neighbourhood piece `D(h z)` of the chart, and a global section `sec z ∈ K` — the
candidate local generator.  The two `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed are
`ThetaGeneratorSeed.IsGenerator`. -/
structure ThetaGeneratorSeed (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (R : Type u) [CommRing R]
    [Algebra k R] (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π] (a : ℕ)
    (K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)) : Type u where
  /-- The pinned chart side of the piece at `z`. -/
  side : relCurve C R → Bool
  /-- The basic-open generator of the piece at `z`. -/
  h : ∀ z : relCurve C R, Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π (side z))
  /-- The point lies in its piece. -/
  mem_basicOpen : ∀ z : relCurve C R, z ∈ (relCurve C R).basicOpen (h z)
  /-- The candidate local generator at `z`. -/
  sec : relCurve C R → relThetaSections C R π a
  /-- The candidate generators are drawn from `K`. -/
  sec_mem : ∀ z, sec z ∈ K

namespace ThetaGeneratorSeed

variable {K : Submodule R (relThetaSections C R π a)} (D : ThetaGeneratorSeed C R π a K)

/-- The neighbourhood piece at `z`: the basic open `D(h z)` of the pinned chart. -/
noncomputable def piece (z : relCurve C R) : (relCurve C R).Opens :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen (D.h z)

lemma mem_piece (z : relCurve C R) : z ∈ D.piece z := D.mem_basicOpen z

lemma piece_le (z : relCurve C R) : D.piece z ≤ relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z) :=
  (relCurve C R).basicOpen_le (D.h z)

/-- The pieces are affine (basic opens of the affine pinned charts). -/
lemma isAffineOpen_piece (z : relCurve C R) : IsAffineOpen (D.piece z) :=
  (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)).basicOpen (D.h z)

/-- **Flatness of the piece sections over the test ring** (the (iii)⟹(i) licence). -/
theorem flat_sections_piece (z : relCurve C R) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  flat_sections_basicOpen R (isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z))
    (flat_sections_relPinnedChart C R π (D.side z)) (D.h z)

/-- **The candidate local equation at `z`**: the side component of the chosen generator,
restricted to the piece. -/
noncomputable def eqn (z : relCurve C R) : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z) :=
  relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) (D.sec z)

/-- **The `lm:ctn` clauses on a seed** (Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii) packaged as its output, plus
the fibrewise-regularity input of (iii)⟹(i)):

* `dvd` — the chosen generator generates the subsheaf `K·𝒪` on its piece: the side
  component of every element of `K` is a multiple of the equation (the Nakayama
  neighbourhood clause, produced fibrewise by the P-fib achiever +
  `exists_fibrewise_tmul_ne_zero_of_projective`);
* `fibre_regular` — the equation is a nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre of
  every basic sub-open of the piece (produced by P-fib: the fibre of the equation is a
  nonzero section of an integral curve over `κ(p)`).

Both clauses are stated relative to the test ring only, so the DD-4 base-field-transport
seam moves a single boundary (spec-dd-r §7 risk 2). -/
structure IsGenerator : Prop where
  dvd : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) ⦃ψ : relThetaSections C R π a⦄, ψ ∈ K →
    relThetaResSide a (D.side z) (D.piece_le z) ψ ∈ Ideal.span {D.eqn z}
  fibre_regular : ∀ (z : relCurve C R) (p : PrimeSpectrum R)
      (f : Γ(relCurve C R, D.piece z)),
    ((relCurve C R).resHom ((relCurve C R).basicOpen_le f) (D.eqn z) ⊗ₜ[R]
        (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) ∈
      nonZeroDivisors
        (Γ(relCurve C R, (relCurve C R).basicOpen f) ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamily
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction

/-!
# Finite-adaptation extraction: every local-equation system has a chart adaptation
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d))

Every `LocalEquations` system `d` on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` refines to a
finite chart adaptation `DivisorAdaptation C R π d` (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): the two
pinned charts `V₀ᴿ`, `V₁ᴿ` are affine, so the DAT-1 (1f) affine-refinement engine
(`IsAffineOpen.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction`)
produces, for each chart, a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor
points, with a partition of unity. Reindexing each chart family through `Fintype.equivFin`
gives the `Fin`-indexed `FinCoverData`; the equations are the restrictions of `d`'s
equations at the anchors (comparison unit `1`), regular by `d.regular` through the
refinement subordination.

The **certificate** (`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`) is deliberately NOT part of the
extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra
finiteness/flatness hypothesis on `d` (the object of DD-1c's field dictionary and DAT-B's
coverage step, which supply it separately).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divisorAdaptation` — the extraction: `Nonempty
  (DivisorAdaptation C R π d)` for every `d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **Finite-adaptation extraction** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d), the DAT-1 (1f)
pattern): every local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a finite chart
adaptation. The two pinned charts are affine, so on each the affine-refinement engine
produces a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor points with a
partition of unity; the equations are the anchor equations of `d` restricted to the pieces
(comparison unit `1`), regular through the subordination. The colength certificate is a
separate hypothesis and is not produced here. -/
theorem exists_divisorAdaptation (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Nonempty (DivisorAdaptation C R π d) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι₀, _, f₀, an₀, b₀, hsub₀, hpart₀⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  obtain ⟨ι₁, _, f₁, an₁, b₁, hsub₁, hpart₁⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  set e₀ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₀) ≃ ι₀ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₀).symm with he₀
  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁
  -- the `Fin`-indexed cover data
  set D : FinCoverData C R π :=
    { m₀ := Fintype.card ι₀
      m₁ := Fintype.card ι₁
      h₀ := fun j => f₀ (e₀ j)
      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)
      a₀ := fun j => b₀ (e₀ j)
      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)
      partition₀ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₀ (fun i => b₀ i * f₀ i)).trans hpart₀
      partition₁ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₁ (fun i => b₁ i * f₁ i)).trans hpart₁ } with hD
  -- the anchor of each piece and its subordination to a member of `d.cover`
  set pt : D.index → relCurve C R :=
    Sum.elim (fun j => an₀ (e₀ j)) (fun j => an₁ (e₁ j)) with hpt
  have hle : ∀ j : D.index, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) := by
    rintro (j | j)
    · exact hsub₀ (e₀ j)
    · exact hsub₁ (e₁ j)
  exact ⟨DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors D
    (fun j => ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hle j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
    pt hle (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul])⟩

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamily
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction

/-!
# Finite-adaptation extraction: every local-equation system has a chart adaptation
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d))

Every `LocalEquations` system `d` on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` refines to a
finite chart adaptation `DivisorAdaptation C R π d` (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): the two
pinned charts `V₀ᴿ`, `V₁ᴿ` are affine, so the DAT-1 (1f) affine-refinement engine
(`IsAffineOpen.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction`)
produces, for each chart, a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor
points, with a partition of unity. Reindexing each chart family through `Fintype.equivFin`
gives the `Fin`-indexed `FinCoverData`; the equations are the restrictions of `d`'s
equations at the anchors (comparison unit `1`), regular by `d.regular` through the
refinement subordination.

The **certificate** (`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`) is deliberately NOT part of the
extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra
finiteness/flatness hypothesis on `d` (the object of DD-1c's field dictionary and DAT-B's
coverage step, which supply it separately).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divisorAdaptation` — the extraction: `Nonempty
  (DivisorAdaptation C R π d)` for every `d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **Finite-adaptation extraction** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d), the DAT-1 (1f)
pattern): every local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a finite chart
adaptation. The two pinned charts are affine, so on each the affine-refinement engine
produces a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor points with a
partition of unity; the equations are the anchor equations of `d` restricted to the pieces
(comparison unit `1`), regular through the subordination. The colength certificate is a
separate hypothesis and is not produced here. -/
theorem exists_divisorAdaptation (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Nonempty (DivisorAdaptation C R π d) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι₀, _, f₀, an₀, b₀, hsub₀, hpart₀⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  obtain ⟨ι₁, _, f₁, an₁, b₁, hsub₁, hpart₁⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  set e₀ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₀) ≃ ι₀ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₀).symm with he₀
  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁
  -- the `Fin`-indexed cover data
  set D : FinCoverData C R π :=
    { m₀ := Fintype.card ι₀
      m₁ := Fintype.card ι₁
      h₀ := fun j => f₀ (e₀ j)
      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)
      a₀ := fun j => b₀ (e₀ j)
      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)
      partition₀ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₀ (fun i => b₀ i * f₀ i)).trans hpart₀
      partition₁ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₁ (fun i => b₁ i * f₁ i)).trans hpart₁ } with hD
  -- the anchor of each piece and its subordination to a member of `d.cover`
  set pt : D.index → relCurve C R :=
    Sum.elim (fun j => an₀ (e₀ j)) (fun j => an₁ (e₁ j)) with hpt
  have hle : ∀ j : D.index, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) := by
    rintro (j | j)
    · exact hsub₀ (e₀ j)
    · exact hsub₁ (e₁ j)
  exact ⟨DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors D
    (fun j => ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hle j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
    pt hle (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul])⟩

end AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The flatness ladder: section rings of basic opens are flat over the test ring -/

section BasicOpenFlat

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]

/-- **Flatness descends to basic opens**: for an affine open `V` with `Γ(X, V)` flat over
the base ring `K`, the section ring of any basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` is flat over `K` —
`Γ(X, D(f))` is a localization of `Γ(X, V)` (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`),
localizations are flat, and flatness composes along the scalar tower
`K → Γ(X, V) → Γ(X, D(f))`. -/
theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hflat : Module.Flat K Γ(X, V)) (f : Γ(X, V)) :
    Module.Flat K Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
  haveI := hflat
  haveI := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen f
  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers f)
  haveI : IsScalarTower K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r =>
      (X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res K (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)).op r).symm
  exact Module.Flat.trans K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f)

end BasicOpenFlat

/-! ## Section-level and unit-ratio consequences of germwise regularity -/

section GermRegular

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

/-- A section all of whose germs are nonzerodivisors is a nonzerodivisor
(sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their germs). -/
theorem sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ {W : X.Opens} {s : Γ(X, W)}
    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)) :
    s ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
  intro t ht
  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
  intro y hy
  rw [map_zero]
  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s = 0 := by
    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
  exact (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (hreg y hy)).mp key

/-- **Mutual divisibility against a germwise-regular section is a unit ratio**: if
`s = c₁ · t` and `t = c₂ · s` with every germ of `s` a nonzerodivisor, then `c₁` is a
unit, so `s = u · t` — the ratio-unit engine of the local-generator construction. -/
theorem exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd {W : X.Opens} {s t c₁ c₂ : Γ(X, W)}
    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))
    (h₁ : s = c₁ * t) (h₂ : t = c₂ * s) :
    ∃ u : Γ(X, W)ˣ, s = (u : Γ(X, W)) * t := by
  have hzero : (1 - c₁ * c₂) * s = 0 := by
    rw [sub_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, ← h₂, ← h₁, sub_self]
  have hone : c₁ * c₂ = 1 := by
    have h := (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff
      (sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ hreg)).mp hzero
    rwa [sub_eq_zero, eq_comm] at h
  exact ⟨Units.mkOfMulEqOne c₁ c₂ hone, h₁⟩

end GermRegular

/-! ## The pinned chart of a side and the side-uniform theta components -/

section Sides

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsFinite π]

/-- The pinned chart of a side: `V₀ᴿ` for `false`, `V₁ᴿ` for `true`. -/
noncomputable def relPinnedChart : Bool → (relCurve C R).Opens
  | false => (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
  | true => (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁

@[simp]
lemma relPinnedChart_false :
    relPinnedChart C R π false = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ := rfl

@[simp]
lemma relPinnedChart_true :
    relPinnedChart C R π true = (relCover C R (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := rfl

/-- Both pinned charts are affine. -/
lemma isAffineOpen_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) : IsAffineOpen (relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
  cases b
  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)
  · exact relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)

/-- **Flatness of the pinned chart sections over the test ring**: `Γ(C_R, Vᵢᴿ)` is the
free base change `R ⊗[k] Γ(C, Vᵢ)` (`free_relSections`), hence flat. -/
theorem flat_sections_relPinnedChart (b : Bool) :
    Module.Flat R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b) := by
  cases b
  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π false) :=
      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₀ π)
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isCompact
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 0).isQuasiSeparated
    exact Module.Flat.of_free
  · haveI : Module.Free R Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π true) :=
      free_relSections C R (fiberChart₁ π)
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isCompact
        (isAffineOpen_preimage_chartOpen π 1).isQuasiSeparated
    exact Module.Flat.of_free

variable {C R π}
variable (a : ℕ)

11	# Canonical syzygies in a high-window multiplication presentation
12	
13	The high-window relation criterion is deliberately stated with a residue-fibre
14	kernel-spanning hypothesis.  This file constructs the canonical candidate, the
15	actual kernel of the multiplication presentation, proves it finite, and identifies
16	its spanning condition with fibrewise injectivity of the injectivized map.
17	
18	Flatness of the target cokernel implies that condition.  Conversely, the landed
19	flattening criterion shows that the condition implies target-cokernel flatness.
20	Consequently, merely choosing the actual kernel does not evade the nonreduced-base
21	gate: its fibre-spanning law is equivalent to the flatness one is trying to prove.
22	No fibrewise image-persistence statement is used as a substitute for this law.
23	-/

58	    LinearMap.ker (f.rTensor A) ≤
59	        LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker f).subtype.rTensor A) ↔
60	      Function.Injective
61	        (((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A) := by
62	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
63	  have hcomp : f.rTensor A =
64	      (L.liftQ f le_rfl).rTensor A ∘ₗ L.mkQ.rTensor A := by
65	    rw [← LinearMap.rTensor_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
66	  have hexact : Function.Exact (L.subtype.rTensor A) (L.mkQ.rTensor A) :=
67	    rTensor_exact A (LinearMap.exact_subtype_mkQ L) (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L)
68	  constructor
69	  · intro hspan
70	    rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
71	    intro w hw
72	    obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.rTensor_surjective A
73	      (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
74	    have hfx : f.rTensor A x = 0 := by
75	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
76	      exact hw
77	    have hx := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
78	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker] at hx
79	    exact hx
80	  · intro hinj x hx
81	    have hzero : L.mkQ.rTensor A x = 0 := by
82	      apply hinj
83	      rw [map_zero]
84	      have hfx := LinearMap.mem_ker.mp hx
85	      rw [hcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply] at hfx
86	      exact hfx
87	    rw [← LinearMap.exact_iff.mp hexact, LinearMap.mem_ker]
88	    exact hzero

91	
92	/-- An independent boundary presentation of every base-changed kernel makes
93	the injectivized map remain injective after that base change.  This is the
94	non-circular bridge from a fibrewise Koszul theorem to the relative flatness
95	criterion: no flatness of the cokernel is assumed.
96	
97	The proof lifts through the right-exact base change of `ker(f).mkQ`.  A lift
98	in the fibre kernel is a base-changed boundary by `hspan`, and the global
99	identity `f ∘ d = 0` makes its quotient class vanish. -/
100	theorem liftQ_baseChange_injective_of_boundary
101	    (f : M →ₗ[R] N) (d : P →ₗ[R] M) (hfd : f.comp d = 0)
102	    (S : Type u) [CommRing S] [Algebra R S]
103	    (hspan : LinearMap.ker (LinearMap.baseChange S f) ≤
104	      LinearMap.range (LinearMap.baseChange S d)) :
105	    Function.Injective
106	      (LinearMap.baseChange S ((LinearMap.ker f).liftQ f le_rfl)) := by
107	  let L := LinearMap.ker f
108	  let fbar := L.liftQ f le_rfl
109	  have hfcomp : LinearMap.baseChange S f =
110	      (LinearMap.baseChange S fbar).comp (LinearMap.baseChange S L.mkQ) := by
111	    rw [← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, Submodule.liftQ_mkQ]
112	  have hdL : ∀ y : P, d y ∈ L := by
113	    intro y
114	    apply LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr
115	    have hy := LinearMap.congr_fun hfd y
116	    simpa only [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply] using hy
117	  have hqd : L.mkQ.comp d = 0 := by
118	    apply LinearMap.ext
119	    intro y
120	    rw [LinearMap.comp_apply, LinearMap.zero_apply, Submodule.mkQ_apply,
121	      Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero]
122	    exact hdL y
123	  rw [injective_iff_map_eq_zero]
124	  intro w hw
125	  obtain ⟨x, rfl⟩ := LinearMap.baseChange_surjective S
126	    (Submodule.mkQ_surjective L) w
127	  have hfx : LinearMap.baseChange S f x = 0 := by
128	    rw [hfcomp, LinearMap.comp_apply]
129	    exact hw
130	  obtain ⟨y, hy⟩ := hspan (LinearMap.mem_ker.mpr hfx)
131	  rw [← hy, ← LinearMap.comp_apply, ← LinearMap.baseChange_comp, hqd,
132	    LinearMap.baseChange_zero, LinearMap.zero_apply]

136	/-- Flatness of the target cokernel forces the fibre kernel to be generated by
137	the base-changed global kernel.  Indeed, the injectivization
138	`M ⧸ ker δ → N` has cokernel `N ⧸ range δ`; flatness of that cokernel makes the
139	injectivization universally injective. -/
140	theorem ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_of_flat_range_quotient
141	    (δ : M →ₗ[R] N)
142	    [Module.Flat R (N ⧸ LinearMap.range δ)]
143	    (A : Type u) [AddCommGroup A] [Module R A] :
144	    LinearMap.ker (δ.rTensor A) ≤
145	      LinearMap.range ((LinearMap.ker δ).subtype.rTensor A) := by
146	  apply (ker_rTensor_le_range_subtype_iff_liftQ_rTensor_injective δ A).mpr
147	  set fbar := (LinearMap.ker δ).liftQ δ le_rfl with hfbar
148	  have hfbar_inj : Function.Injective fbar := by
149	    rw [← LinearMap.ker_eq_bot, hfbar]
150	    exact Submodule.ker_liftQ_eq_bot' _ δ rfl
151	  have hexact : Function.Exact fbar (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ := by
152	    rw [LinearMap.exact_iff, Submodule.ker_mkQ, hfbar, Submodule.range_liftQ]
153	  have hleft : Function.Injective (fbar.lTensor A) :=
154	    LinearMap.lTensor_injective_of_exact_of_flat
155	      (LinearMap.range δ).mkQ (Submodule.mkQ_surjective _)
156	      fbar hfbar_inj hexact A
157	  exact (LinearMap.lTensor_inj_iff_rTensor_inj (M := A) (f := fbar)).mp hleft
158	
159	end KernelSpan

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FibrewiseRegular
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.FlatCokernel
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.Tensor
import Mathlib.RingTheory.Flat.EquationalCriterion

/-!
# The slicing criterion, flat-quotient form (Kleiman `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i), the Tor half)

**The third Tor-lemma home** of the DAT-D campaign, completing the pair
`Picard/FibrewiseRegular` (fibrewise-regular + flat ⟹ regular) and
`Picard/FlatCokernel` (regular + flat quotient ⟹ regular after any base change):

> over a Noetherian ring `R`, if `B` is a flat `R`-algebra and `f ∈ B` is a
> nonzerodivisor in every residue-field fibre `B ⊗[R] κ(p)`, then the quotient
> `B ⧸ (f)` is **flat** over `R`.

This is the missing flat-QUOTIENT conclusion of Kleiman's `lm:ctn`
(`references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex` 1786–1815): the paper's
`Tor₁(B/(f), κ) = 0` computation is replaced by the ideal criterion of flatness plus the
Noetherian ideal-division engine already underlying `FibrewiseRegular`. Concretely, for
`Q = coker φ` of an endomorphism `φ` of a flat module `M`, injectivity of the canonical
map `I ⊗ Q → Q` is chased through the right-exact ladder `I ⊗ M → I ⊗ Q` using only

* injectivity of `I ⊗ M → M` (flatness of `M`, `iff_lift_lsmul_comp_subtype_injective`),
* the **ideal-division property** `φ x ∈ I·M ⟹ x ∈ I·M` — which over a Noetherian `R` is
  produced from fibrewise injectivity by the same Noetherian induction (prime fibres +
  flat colon lemma) as `Module.Flat.injective_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective`,
  here exposed as the public `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_apply_mem_smul_top`.

No `Tor`, no local criterion of flatness, no finiteness hypothesis on `B`.

## Main declarations

* `Module.Flat.mem_smul_top_of_apply_mem_smul_top` — the ideal-division engine
  (fibrewise-injective endomorphism of a flat module divides ideal memberships);
* `Module.Flat.of_surjective_exact_of_forall_mem_smul_top` — flatness of a cokernel from
  the ideal-division property (no Noetherian hypothesis);
* `Module.Flat.of_surjective_exact_of_forall_rTensor_residueField_injective` — the
  module-form keystone;
* `Module.Flat.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — **the slicing
  criterion, ring form**: fibrewise-regular + flat `B` over Noetherian `R` ⟹
  `Module.Flat R (B ⧸ Ideal.span {f})` — the DDR-4 certificate clause (c1) flatness
  input on each chart-local colength `Γ(D(h_j)) ⧸ (f_j)`;
* `Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField` — the (c1)
  glue: with `Module.Finite` of the colength (the support-tube input), the colength is
  finite **projective**;
* `Algebra.TensorProduct.includeRight_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_tmul_residueField` —
  the composite with `FlatCokernel`: a fibrewise-regular element of a flat algebra over

  relative-divisibility engine of the seed `dvd` brick, Kleiman (ii)⟹(iii)'s Tor input).
-/

  constructor

      Ideal.Quotient.mkₐ_eq_mk]
    exact (Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem).mpr hmem

/-- **The slicing criterion, ring form** (fibrewise-regular + flat base ⟹ flat
quotient; Kleiman `lm:ctn` (iii)⟹(i), the Tor half; DDR-4 (c1) flatness): over a
Noetherian ring `R`, if `B` is a flat `R`-algebra and the image of `f : B` in every
residue-field fibre `B ⊗[R] κ(p)` is a nonzerodivisor, then the colength `B ⧸ (f)` is
flat over `R`.

Instantiated by DDR-4 at `B = Γ(D(h_j))`, `f =` the adaptation equation `f_j` (the
fibrewise hypothesis is the seed's `fibre_regular` clause transported through
`eqn_rel`); combined with `Module.Finite` (the support tube) it yields the certificate
clause (c1) via `Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField`.
Note the `k[ε]` trap: fibrewise regularity of `f` alone (without flatness of `B`) does
NOT suffice, and the conclusion genuinely fails for non-flat `B`. -/

    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      (f ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : B ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors (B ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
    Module.Flat R (B ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) := by

    (fun y => ?_) (exact_mulLeft_mkQuotient f) (fun p => ?_)

    exact ⟨x, hx⟩

presented as soon as it is finite (the support-tube input), hence projective. -/
theorem Module.Projective.quotient_span_singleton_of_forall_tmul_residueField
    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Flat R B] {f : B}
    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      (f ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : B ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors (B ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))
    [Module.Finite R (B ⧸ Ideal.span {f})] :
    Module.Projective R (B ⧸ Ideal.span {f}) := by

hypothesis on `R'`. Chains the slicing criterion into

    [IsNoetherianRing R] [Module.Flat R B] {f : B}
    (hfib : ∀ p : PrimeSpectrum R,
      (f ⊗ₜ[R] (1 : p.asIdeal.ResidueField) : B ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField) ∈
        nonZeroDivisors (B ⊗[R] p.asIdeal.ResidueField))

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamily
import AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction

/-!
# Finite-adaptation extraction: every local-equation system has a chart adaptation
(`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d))

Every `LocalEquations` system `d` on the relative curve `C_R = relCurve C R` refines to a
finite chart adaptation `DivisorAdaptation C R π d` (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §1a): the two
pinned charts `V₀ᴿ`, `V₁ᴿ` are affine, so the DAT-1 (1f) affine-refinement engine
(`IsAffineOpen.exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement` in
`AlgebraicJacobian.Cohomology.GluedSheafExtraction`)
produces, for each chart, a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor
points, with a partition of unity. Reindexing each chart family through `Fintype.equivFin`
gives the `Fin`-indexed `FinCoverData`; the equations are the restrictions of `d`'s
equations at the anchors (comparison unit `1`), regular by `d.regular` through the
refinement subordination.

The **certificate** (`DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified`) is deliberately NOT part of the
extraction: an adaptation always exists, whereas the colength certificate is an extra
finiteness/flatness hypothesis on `d` (the object of DD-1c's field dictionary and DAT-B's
coverage step, which supply it separately).

* `AlgebraicGeometry.exists_divisorAdaptation` — the extraction: `Nonempty
  (DivisorAdaptation C R π d)` for every `d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations`.
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
variable (π : C.left ⟶ P1 k) [IsAffineHom π]

/-- **Finite-adaptation extraction** (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 stage (d), the DAT-1 (1f)
pattern): every local-equation system on the relative curve refines to a finite chart
adaptation. The two pinned charts are affine, so on each the affine-refinement engine
produces a finite basic-open family subordinated to `d.cover` at anchor points with a
partition of unity; the equations are the anchor equations of `d` restricted to the pieces
(comparison unit `1`), regular through the subordination. The colength certificate is a
separate hypothesis and is not produced here. -/
theorem exists_divisorAdaptation (d : (relCurve C R).LocalEquations) :
    Nonempty (DivisorAdaptation C R π d) := by
  classical
  obtain ⟨ι₀, _, f₀, an₀, b₀, hsub₀, hpart₀⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₀ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  obtain ⟨ι₁, _, f₁, an₁, b₁, hsub₁, hpart₁⟩ :=
    (relCover_isAffineOpen₁ C R (fiberTwoCover π)).exists_finite_basicOpen_refinement d.cover
  set e₀ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₀) ≃ ι₀ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₀).symm with he₀
  set e₁ : Fin (Fintype.card ι₁) ≃ ι₁ := (Fintype.equivFin ι₁).symm with he₁
  -- the `Fin`-indexed cover data
  set D : FinCoverData C R π :=
    { m₀ := Fintype.card ι₀
      m₁ := Fintype.card ι₁
      h₀ := fun j => f₀ (e₀ j)
      h₁ := fun j => f₁ (e₁ j)
      a₀ := fun j => b₀ (e₀ j)
      a₁ := fun j => b₁ (e₁ j)
      partition₀ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₀ (fun i => b₀ i * f₀ i)).trans hpart₀
      partition₁ := (Equiv.sum_comp e₁ (fun i => b₁ i * f₁ i)).trans hpart₁ } with hD
  -- the anchor of each piece and its subordination to a member of `d.cover`
  set pt : D.index → relCurve C R :=
    Sum.elim (fun j => an₀ (e₀ j)) (fun j => an₁ (e₁ j)) with hpt
  have hle : ∀ j : D.index, D.pieces j ≤ d.cover.opens (pt j) := by
    rintro (j | j)
    · exact hsub₀ (e₀ j)
    · exact hsub₁ (e₁ j)
  exact ⟨DivisorAdaptation.ofAnchors D
    (fun j => ((relCurve C R).presheaf.map (homOfLE (hle j)).op).hom (d.eqn (pt j)))
    pt hle (fun _ => 1) (fun _ => by rw [Units.val_one, one_mul])⟩

end AlgebraicGeometry

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyField
import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.OpenImmersionUnits

/-!
# The colength↔degree identity for divisor families over a field (`informal/spec-dd-1.md` §3 (f))

Over a field `K` the forward map `divFamDivisor` (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.DivisorFamilyField`)
sends a certified divisor family to its Weil divisor. This file lands the **degree identity**

`deg K (divFamDivisor F) = finrank K W(d)`

(so, with the field half `DivisorAdaptation.IsCertified.finrank_glued`, `deg = n`), the
colength↔degree bridge across the glued equalizer `W(d) = ker (δ⁻ − δ⁺)`.

## The support-separated assembly

The equalizer does not decompose over the cover naively — a supported closed point may lie in
two pieces. This file proves the **support-separated** case, which is the one the DD-1c backward
map consumes (its adaptations isolate the support points by construction): when the overlap
colength modules vanish (`ovlColength i j` is subsingleton for `i ≠ j`), the equalizer is the
*whole* product of the chart-local colengths, so

`finrank K W(d) = ∑ⱼ finrank K (Γ(D(hⱼ)) ⧸ (fⱼ))`  (`finrank_glued_eq_sum_of_separated`),

pure module algebra (`Module.finrank_pi_fintype` over the field, where every factor is free).
-/

set_option autoImplicit false

universe u

open CategoryTheory TopologicalSpace Opposite
open Module (finrank)

namespace AlgebraicGeometry

/-! ## A unit-germ ↔ trivial-order dictionary on the curve bundle

Reusable core: on the curve bundle `X/K`, a section `f` over an open `U ∋ η` is a unit at a
closed point `z ∈ U` exactly when the order at `z` of its germ at `η` is trivial. Both
directions of the private `ChartColength` machinery, packaged as a public equivalence through
the DVR valuation of the stalk. -/

namespace Scheme

variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]

/-- **Unit germ ↔ trivial order.** For a section `f` over an open `U ∋ η` whose germ at `η` is
the field unit `g`, the germ of `f` at a closed point `z ∈ U` is a unit of the stalk exactly
when the order of `g` at `z` is trivial (`ordZ = 1`). -/
theorem isUnit_germ_iff_ordZ_eq_one {U : X.Opens} (hη : genericPoint X ∈ U)
    (f : Γ(X, U)) (g : X.functionFieldˣ)
    (hg : (g : X.functionField) = (X.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hη).hom f)
    {z : X} (hz : z ∈ U) (hzg : z ≠ genericPoint X) :
    IsUnit ((X.presheaf.germ U z hz).hom f)
      ↔ Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg g = 1 := by
  rw [Scheme.ordZ_eq_one_iff]
  letI := isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg
  letI := isDedekindDomain_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg
  have hord : Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hzg
      = (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField := rfl
  have hgs : (X.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hη).hom f
      = algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField
          ((X.presheaf.germ U z hz).hom f) := by
    rw [RingHom.algebraMap_toAlgebra]
    exact (X.presheaf.germ_stalkSpecializes_apply hz
      ((genericPoint_spec X).specializes trivial) f).symm
  rw [hg, hgs, hord, IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_eq_one_iff_notMem]
  exact (IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal).symm

/-- A unit in a closed-point stalk remains a unit in the function field, hence has
trivial `ordZ`.  This is the valuation form of the stalk-unit transition bridge used
when comparing a pulled local equation with a theta-chart reading. -/
theorem ordZ_unitsMap_stalk_eq_one {z : X} (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X)
    (v : (X.presheaf.stalk z)ˣ) :
    Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
      (Units.map (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField).toMonoidHom v) = 1 := by
  rw [Scheme.ordZ_eq_one_iff (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz]
  exact Valuation.Integers.one_of_isUnit'
    (v := Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz)
    v.isUnit (fun y => Scheme.ord_algebraMap_stalk_le_one K hz y)

/-- Multiplication by the function-field image of a stalk unit does not change the
additive order at the closed point. -/
theorem toAdd_ordZ_mul_unitsMap_stalk {z : X} (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X)
    (a : X.functionFieldˣ) (v : (X.presheaf.stalk z)ˣ) :
    Multiplicative.toAdd
        (Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
          (a * Units.map (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField).toMonoidHom v))
      = Multiplicative.toAdd (Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz a) := by
  rw [map_mul, ordZ_unitsMap_stalk_eq_one K hz v, mul_one]

end Scheme

    (hsep : ∀ i j : A.index, i ≠ j → Subsingleton (A.ovlColength i j)) :

      (A.toOvlLeft_self_eq_toOvlRight_self i)) (s i)
  · haveI := hsep i j hij
    exact Subsingleton.elim _ _

attribute [local instance] Scheme.overModule Scheme.overSectionsAlgebra

/-! ## The flatness ladder: section rings of basic opens are flat over the test ring -/

section BasicOpenFlat

variable (K : Type u) [CommRing K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (.of K))]

/-- **Flatness descends to basic opens**: for an affine open `V` with `Γ(X, V)` flat over
the base ring `K`, the section ring of any basic open `D(f) ⊆ V` is flat over `K` —
`Γ(X, D(f))` is a localization of `Γ(X, V)` (`IsAffineOpen.isLocalization_basicOpen`),
localizations are flat, and flatness composes along the scalar tower
`K → Γ(X, V) → Γ(X, D(f))`. -/
theorem flat_sections_basicOpen {V : X.Opens} (hV : IsAffineOpen V)
    (hflat : Module.Flat K Γ(X, V)) (f : Γ(X, V)) :
    Module.Flat K Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) := by
  haveI := hflat
  haveI := hV.isLocalization_basicOpen f
  haveI : Module.Flat Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f) :=
    IsLocalization.flat _ (Submonoid.powers f)

    IsScalarTower.of_algebraMap_eq fun r =>
      (X.overAlgebraMap_apply_res K (homOfLE (X.basicOpen_le f)).op r).symm

/-! ## Section-level and unit-ratio consequences of germwise regularity -/

section GermRegular

variable {X : Scheme.{u}}

(sections of a sheaf inject into the product of their germs). -/
theorem sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ {W : X.Opens} {s : Γ(X, W)}
    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y)) :
    s ∈ nonZeroDivisors Γ(X, W) := by
  rw [mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_right]
  intro t ht
  apply TopCat.Presheaf.section_ext X.sheaf W t 0
  intro y hy
  rw [map_zero]
  have key : (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom t * (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s = 0 := by
    rw [← map_mul, ht, map_zero]
  exact (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff (hreg y hy)).mp key

/-- **Mutual divisibility against a germwise-regular section is a unit ratio**: if
`s = c₁ · t` and `t = c₂ · s` with every germ of `s` a nonzerodivisor, then `c₁` is a

theorem exists_unit_mul_of_mutual_dvd {W : X.Opens} {s t c₁ c₂ : Γ(X, W)}
    (hreg : ∀ (y : X) (hy : y ∈ W),
      (X.presheaf.germ W y hy).hom s ∈ nonZeroDivisors (X.presheaf.stalk y))
    (h₁ : s = c₁ * t) (h₂ : t = c₂ * s) :
    ∃ u : Γ(X, W)ˣ, s = (u : Γ(X, W)) * t := by
  have hzero : (1 - c₁ * c₂) * s = 0 := by
    rw [sub_mul, one_mul, mul_assoc, ← h₂, ← h₁, sub_self]
  have hone : c₁ * c₂ = 1 := by
    have h := (mul_right_mem_nonZeroDivisors_eq_zero_iff
      (sections_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_forall_germ hreg)).mp hzero
    rwa [sub_eq_zero, eq_comm] at h

  exact Module.Flat.trans K Γ(X, V) Γ(X, X.basicOpen f)

end BasicOpenFlat

  exact ⟨Units.mkOfMulEqOne c₁ c₂ hone, h₁⟩

end GermRegular
